copies.headline: Juwan Johnson Beats Noah By Himself
copies.body:
The tight end spot decided this, and it wasn't close. Juwan Johnson put up 23.3 for Grant; Terrance Ferguson gave Noah 1.9 on a 10.6 projection. That 21.4-point gap is more than four times the final margin, and it swallowed everything Noah did right — he won running back by 14.3, won receiver, won the flex, and still lost by 4.9. Drake Maye's 3.8 in a week he was projected for 18.6 didn't help, and De'Von Achane turning 19.4 of projection into 1.7 was the kind of morning that makes you stop refreshing.
The bench was the real crime. Michael Wilson scored 25.9 in street clothes while Mike Evans managed 12.4. Start Wilson, Noah wins by nine. Our preview had Noah by 7, which now looks charitable.
Noah is 0-3 with an all-play of 2-31 and 83.0 points a game, dead last in both. The postseason assassin has three months to find a pulse. Grant is 2-1 on 84.4 points, which is theft, but he's cashed worse checks.

copies.headline: Isaac Wins Everywhere Except Quarterback
copies.body:
The mechanism here was CJ losing six of seven lineup spots. Tyler Shough's 23.8 gave him a twelve-point quarterback edge and that was the entire case for the defense — Isaac countered with plus-7.1 at running back, plus-8.2 at receiver, plus-4.8 in the flex, and a ten-point win at kicker, because Chris Boswell kicked field goals while Ka'imi Fairbairn apparently watched. Add it up and you get 23.2 without anyone on Isaac's roster doing anything heroic.
CJ's actual problem was the middle of his lineup. Jonathan Taylor came in at 20.6 projected and delivered 9.2, Hunter Henry turned 10.1 into 1.5 with Jake Ferguson and his 9.3 sitting on the bench, and a 97.9 is his season low by twenty points. Isaac won this while leaving Bo Nix (24.1), Kalif Raymond (21.0) and Terry McLaurin (19.7) benched, which tells you how little he needed to be right.
Both sit 2-1, but Isaac is 11th in scoring with a 9-24 all-play, so nobody should mistake this for a corner turned. We had CJ by 17, which now reads as generous.

copies.headline: John's Receivers Vanish, Kaleb Wins By Eleven
copies.body:
This one came down to wideouts, and it wasn't close. Kaleb got 39.0 from Drake London and Ladd McConkey; John got 7.0 from Brian Thomas Jr. and Dontayvion Wicks combined. Thomas managed 1.8 on a 10.7 projection, which is the entire margin and then some. John won the QB spot, the backfield and the flex — Kyren Williams 21.8, Brock Bowers 27.6, Stafford 20.9 — and still lost by 11.2, because two starting receivers produced less than his defense.
Kaleb didn't exactly play a clean game either. Breece Hall (8.5 on 16.2) and Ashton Jeanty (12.3 on 18.9) both came up short, and Kenyon Sadiq put up 23.5 on the bench while Carnell Tate managed 11.8. Harold Fannin Jr.'s 24.1 and the Vikings' 19.0 covered for all of it. We had Kaleb by 11; he won by 11.2.
John's now 1-2 at 120.9 a game, fourth in scoring, minus-0.6 in luck. He's losing games he's earning, which is a worse feeling than being bad.

copies.headline: Adam's Receivers Bury Leif's Backfield
copies.body:
The wideouts settled this. Jaxon Smith-Njigba went for 35.4 and Chris Olave added 19.7, giving Adam 55.1 at receiver against Leif's 28.0 — a 27.1-point gap that no amount of Derrick Henry could close. Leif actually won the backfield 43.5 to 29.1, got 10.0 from the Texans defense while Adam's Eagles unit posted a minus-1.0, and still lost by 21.5. That's what happens when Brock Purdy hangs 31.3 and Josh Allen answers with 17.5, six under his projection.
Adam won this on his worst day of the year. 142.9 is his season low and he still cleared Leif's 121.5 comfortably, even with Jalen Coker turning 13.8 of projection into 3.8 and Bucky Irving stopping at 7.8. Leif's problem was the middle: Stefon Diggs 7.3, Dalton Schultz 6.0, David Montgomery 6.8. Three roster spots, 20.1 points.
Adam is 3-0 with a 31-2 all-play, which is less a hot start than a warning. We had him by 12. Leif, 2-1 and second in scoring, is having the best season of his life and has nothing to show for it.

copies.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs Buries Christian's Perfect Start
copies.body:
The running back slot decided this and it wasn't close. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 41.4 by himself — more than Christian's entire backfield, which came in at 23.1 between Chase Brown and Aaron Jones Sr. That's a 29.4-point hole at one position, and Christian spent the rest of the afternoon trying to climb out with a tight end. George Kittle's 26.2 clawed back 11.5 of it, but every other slot was a coin flip decided by a point or two. Mitchell won the one that mattered by 30.
Chase Brown was the killer: 8.9 on a 16.6 projection, with Bhayshul Tuten putting up 17.0 in street clothes. That's a 16-point swing available to anyone reading a depth chart. Mitchell had his own sin — Sam Darnold's 27.7 rotting on the bench behind Dak Prescott's 18.9 — but you can afford mistakes when your RB1 outscores half the league's starting lineups. We picked Christian by 16 and got the margin right, just pointed the wrong direction.
Christian is 0-3 while scoring 127.0 a game, third in the league, with an all-play of 19-14 and 1.7 wins evaporated to schedule. That's not a bad team, that's a haunted one. Mitchell, meanwhile, has scored 73 and 149 in consecutive weeks, which is the most Mitchell thing imaginable.

copies.headline: Logan's Receivers Post 8.9, Season Continues
copies.body:
The wide receiver room decided this before lunch. Peter got 21.0 from Tee Higgins and 7.9 from Romeo Doubs; Logan got 5.2 from Justin Jefferson and 3.7 from Tetairoa McMillan, a combined 8.9 against projections of 18.3 and 14.2. Add Isaiah Likely turning 12.2 projected into 3.3 and the Packers defense going negative-six, and Logan was down roughly 31 points at two spots before anyone's stars showed up. Bijan Robinson's 35.3 for Peter was gravy on a meal already cooked.
Logan actually had the better flex — Luther Burden III's 19.8 beat George Pickens — and Jeremiyah Love's 21.9 was legitimate. Didn't matter. Peter's only real sin was starting Kyle Monangai for 3.1 while Chris Rodriguez Jr. put up 9.7 on the bench, which is the kind of mistake you can afford in a 43.8-point win. Our preview had Logan by 9, which now reads as optimism.
Peter's 3-0 comes with a 48% all-play and +1.5 luck wins, so temper the parade. Logan is 0-3 with the league's tenth-best scoring and a dress still fresh in memory.

intro: Mitchell's 149.24 was the week's high-water mark and it still only bought an 18-point win over Christian, which tells you how much scoring went around on a slate where Noah and Grant combined for 164. Adam and Kaleb both cleared 130 to knock off teams that would have won four of the other five matchups, while Peter turned in the only genuine beatdown, hanging 126.34 on a Logan roster that managed 82.52 and never threatened. Grant escaped by 4.9 in a game neither team especially deserved to win.
